clue.text: When retiring, mother takes hot baths

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the mother-plus-hot string is read from right to left

parts.note: mamma is a familiar word for mother
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Mum goes off to bed and first has a hot soak in the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When retiring' turns the whole string MAMMAH round. 'Baths' works here as a singular noun, as in 'the public baths'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammam is a Turkish steam bathhouse, so it is a set of baths in the public-baths sense.

clue.text: Greek historian turned out in Rhodes, possibly

indicators.note: turned out reads as an anagram signal: the letters of out and Rhodes are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek writer of history turns up on the island of Rhodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' joins the two fodder words and 'possibly' marks the surface as speculative. Rhodes is a Greek island, which makes the picture convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Herodotus, writing in the fifth century BC, is called the father of history and was Greek.

clue.text: Disadvantage of millions across the pond

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)
across the pond means over the Atlantic, in the United States: in US

explanation.surface: A drawback suffered by millions of Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: A minus, as in 'pluses and minuses', is a drawback or negative point.

clue.text: One's sorry to say this guy appears gutted after a game

indicators.note: after places the trimmed guy behind the a-plus-game pieces

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: a gutted fish has its insides removed, so only the first and last letters of guy stay

explanation.surface: A man looks thoroughly fed up after losing a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' looks like British slang for very disappointed, which fits a lost game, but it strips guy to GY.
explanation.definitionFit: An apology is the statement a person makes to express regret.

clue.text: They keep medicines, note, in sturdy containers

indicators.note: in tells us the note sits inside the containers

parts.note: chests are strong boxes for storage
mi (or me) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Pharmacists store their drugs, take note, in strong boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists, the British word for pharmacists or drugstores, stock and dispense medicines.

clue.text: Even Irish types could become so touchy

indicators.note: could become signals the letters of the three words being made into something new

explanation.surface: Even the Irish sort might get very prickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypersensitive means excessively easily offended, which is being touchy to a high degree, as 'so' implies.

clue.text: Communist group occupying public transport during revolution

indicators.note: revolution means turning round, so the combined letters are read backwards
occupying means the group sits inside the transport word

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle of public transport
a six is a group of six, such as a unit of Brownies or Cubs

explanation.surface: A party cell takes over the trams in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' looks like the communist uprising of the surface but is the reversal signal on TSIXRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A Marxist follows the doctrines of Karl Marx, the founder of communism.

clue.text: After eating up egg, one looks drunk perhaps

indicators.note: eating means the looker takes the turned egg inside

parts.note: a starer is someone who looks hard

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word egg is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone stares after swallowing an egg, apparently intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like the adjective describing the one who looks, but with 'perhaps' it defines by example. 'Up' turns the egg backwards before the looker swallows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has drunk too much walks unsteadily, so a drunk is one example of a person who reels.

clue.text: Spicy dish always served at end of day

indicators.note: served at end of places always behind the day

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday, a day
ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A hot meal is always dished up as the day closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of day' wants to give Y, but the day is SAT and 'always' sits at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is a Southeast Asian dish of skewered meat in a spiced peanut sauce.

clue.text: Beryl and Ruby maybe arranged P & O cruises to most parts of the globe?

indicators.note: arranged signals the letters of P & O cruises are set in a new order

parts.note: P & O is the cruise and ferry line, giving the letters P and O
three of the four compass points, north, east and south, make up most of the points of the globe

explanation.surface: Two women book a cruise line trip to almost everywhere in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Beryl and Ruby look like women's names but are gems. 'Arranged' rearranges the cruise line and its trips into the first word plus one S; the compass points north, east and south finish it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl and ruby are both gems of high value, examples of the category.

clue.text: Animosity in Tommy's report

indicators.note: report means a sound, so the word for the soldier is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Tommy (Atkins) is slang for a British private soldier, one in the ranks, a ranker

explanation.surface: Bitterness shows in a British soldier's dispatch.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is a British private soldier, and a ranker is a soldier who has not been commissioned; in a non-rhotic accent ranker and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated bitterness or ill will, the same as animosity.

clue.text: Rich dessert: portion stuffed with tiny slice of fruit's best

indicators.note: stuffed with means the portion word has the other letters packed inside it

parts.note: a part is a portion

indicators.note: a tiny slice is just a single letter, the first of fruit

parts.note: A1, written AI in crosswords, means first-rate or best

explanation.surface: A rich pudding: a helping filled with a sliver of the finest fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: AI stands for A1, the best grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A parfait is a frozen dessert of cream, eggs and fruit, so it is a rich pudding.

clue.text: Record being played at church by rector causing a sensation, in off-putting way

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a record being played is on
CE is the Church of England
tingly describes a prickling sensation

explanation.surface: A record played in church by the vicar makes a stir, unsettlingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconcertingly means in an unsettling manner, which is off-putting.

clue.text: Merry end to day after barbecue's over

indicators.note: after puts the barbecue word ahead of the letter it follows
over means turned over, so the spit word is read backwards

parts.note: a spit is a rod for roasting meat at a barbecue

indicators.note: end to day means the last letter of day

explanation.surface: Feeling jolly when the day ends once the barbecue is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reverses SPIT to TIPS. Merry is British for slightly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy means slightly drunk, the same tone as merry after a few drinks.

clue.text: Cook polenta with it, showing hidden talent

indicators.note: to cook something is to alter it, as one cooks the books, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Making polenta reveals someone's latent gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Potential is ability not yet realised, a latent capacity.

clue.text: Public controversy about Henry's defeat

indicators.note: about means the public-row string goes round the henry letter

parts.note: overt means open or public
a row is a noisy dispute
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: An open dispute about a king called Henry ends in his downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: An overthrow is the toppling of a ruler or government, a decisive defeat.

clue.text: One dam, then another, sited close to loch? That's strange

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river

indicators.note: close means end, so take the final letter of sited

parts.note: Ness is the most famous loch in Scotland

explanation.surface: Two dams side by side near a Scottish lake look odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Then another' only adds to the surface; it gives no letters. Loch Ness is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Weirdness is oddness, the quality of being strange, which 'that's strange' points to.

clue.text: More than one humorous writer is in dire straits

indicators.note: in places the word is inside the shuffled letters
dire means terrible, so the letters of straits are put in a mess

explanation.surface: Several comic authors find themselves in desperate need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dire straits' reads as a single phrase for desperate trouble, but 'dire' is the anagram signal, giving SATIRTS, and 'in' places the clue's own 'is' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Satirists mock folly through humour, so they are plural humorous writers.

clue.text: Writer found grumbling no good

indicators.note: no means the good letter is removed

parts.note: growling is grumbling or complaining

explanation.surface: An author is discovered to be complaining without any merit.
explanation.walkthrough: J. K. Rowling is the author of the Harry Potter books.
explanation.definitionFit: J. K. Rowling is a famous British author, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Officer and soldier guarding queen's dog

indicators.note: guarding means the two military words surround the queen letter

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
GI is an American soldier
R is short for regina, queen

explanation.surface: Military men keep watch over the monarch's pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the corgis kept by Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog.

clue.text: Swindler, say, on a horse — a fast-moving animal

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after, so the swindler comes first
say means as heard, so the swindler word is spoken

parts.note: a cheat is a swindler
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A conman, say, mounted on a horse makes a quick getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, a big cat of Africa.

clue.text: Film broadcast on Wed night about origins of Calendar Girls?

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters surround the institute
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of on Wed night are spread anew

parts.note: the Calendar Girls were members of the WI, the Women's Institute, which gave rise to their story

explanation.surface: A movie shown on Wednesday night about the women behind a famous charity calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: The Calendar Girls were Yorkshire members of the Women's Institute (the WI), a British women's organisation, who posed nude for a charity calendar. 'Broadcast' shuffles ON WED NIGHT into GONEWITHND around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1939 epic set in the American Civil War is one of the most famous movies.

clue.text: Newlywed given key to boudoir, say

parts.note: G is a musical key
a boudoir is an example of a room

explanation.surface: A just-married man is handed the key to the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Groom, short for bridegroom, is a man just married or about to be.

clue.text: Fellow's words when taking the plunge?

explanation.surface: A man exclaims as he dives in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo is a man's name, as in the architect Inigo Jones; read as three words it is what a swimmer might say before jumping into water.

clue.text: View servant heading off after work

indicators.note: after puts the beheaded servant behind the work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a minion is a servile follower

explanation.surface: Seeing a servant leave once the job is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is one's view on a matter.

clue.text: Display case: see it in exhibition primarily? That's about right

indicators.note: about means the other pieces wrap round the right letter

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so the first letter of exhibition

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cabinet in an exhibition is mainly there to be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'see' comes from vide in references.
explanation.definitionFit: A vitrine is a glass-fronted cabinet for showing objects.

clue.text: Perhaps inhabitant of Kuala Lumpur about to prattle in foreign language

indicators.note: about means the inhabitant word goes round the prattle

parts.note: a Malay is a typical inhabitant of the Malaysian capital
gas is idle chatter

explanation.surface: A Malaysian is about to chatter away in an unfamiliar tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container signal and 'to' a link. Kuala Lumpur is the capital of Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: Malagasy is the language of Madagascar, foreign to English speakers.

clue.text: Wife rings? Oh dear!

parts.note: hoops are rings

explanation.surface: Is the wife phoning? How awkward!
explanation.definitionFit: Whoops is an exclamation of mild dismay at a mistake.
